newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Four pct of Brazil soybean crop harvested - Safras.
newsitem.headline: Four pct of Brazil soybean crop harvested - Safras.

text.p: Despite earlier-than-usual planting this year, only four percent of Brazil's 1996/97 soybean crop had been harvested by the week ending Feb 20, independent consultants Safras e Mercado said.
"(This is) practically within the norm for the period, which has averaged three percent over the last five years," Safras said in a weekly report.
"Despite planting having begun earlier than last year, it should be taken into account that the bulk of the harvest is still in March and April," it added.
Most of the crop was now in the grain formation and maturing phase.

"It is important to note that the rains from this last week of February onwards need to be more spaced out in order to avoid problems which have until now been localised from reaching truly preoccupying proportions," Safras said.
The situation in the main growing regions was as follows:

-- PARANA: Despite delay in harvest of early-cycle crop due to rains, crop is in good to excellent condition. Losses limited to isolated areas in west of state. Steady climate vital from now on as much of crop in final development phase.

-- RIO GRANDE DO SUL: Regular rains in last two weeks have produced ideal conditions. Productivity forecasts back to levels seen before dry spell in December/January. Missions area to begin harvesting mid-March but rest of state in April.

-- MATO GROSSO: Rains also delayed harvest of early-cycle crop. Modest productivity losses registered, mostly in north and centre-north. Rains have also damaged roads, possibly complicating the shipment of new crop.

-- MATO GROSSO DO SUL: Improvement in weather gave growers breathing space in centre-south where crop ready for harvesting. Losses considered minimal. Good soil moisture strongly favoured normal-cycle crop with average productivity seen high.
-- GOIAS: Climate improved although rains remain regular. Some losses among early-cycle crop in south-west. More sun and less rain needed.

-- MINAS GERAIS: Return of sunshine in February improved conditions especially as rains normalised. Good productivity prospects with harvest due to start at end of March. ((--Joelle Diderich, Sao Paulo newsroom +55 11 248 5417))
